short.en: when you look at a flat before you rent it

def.en: We are going to a flat viewing because we are interested in the flat.

short.en: very beautiful

def.en: She says that the holiday was wonderful.

short.en: a small sausage

def.en: I eat a warm sausage.

short.en: calm exercises for the body and the mind

def.en: She says that yoga helps her relax.

short.en: a device that measures how much electricity, water or gas you use

def.en: The technician reads the meter because the annual bill is coming.

short.en: the person who receives the money in a transfer

def.en: I ask who the payee is.

short.en: how you organise your time well

def.en: He says that good time management is important.

short.en: a text in a newspaper

def.en: She says that this newspaper article is very interesting.

short.en: for a certain time, not always

def.en: The road is temporarily closed because construction work is going on there.

short.en: to get food ready for cooking

def.en: I prepare the food because the guests are coming soon.

def.en: I buy a fresh courgette.

def.en: We need a new access because the door is broken.

short.en: an office where you register a car

def.en: I ask where the vehicle registration office is.

def.en: I like to watch because the game is exciting.

def.en: The price is plus tax because that is required by law.

short.en: sometimes, between two activities

def.en: I eat an apple in between because I am hungry.

task.en:
You are new at the company and today is your first working day. You would like to get to know the team and the boss. A colleague helps you.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (time)
Where? (meeting room, canteen)
Whom first? (team, boss)

q.en: Good morning! I'm Nina and today is my first day at the company. I <g>haven't met</g> the team and the boss yet. Can you help me?

a.en:
Sure, no problem. I'm David.
We could start at nine o'clock, because all the colleagues will be here then.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just start in the canteen?

a1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the canteen doesn't open until eleven.
We could do it like this: we meet in the meeting room and I bring coffee.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that we greet the team first and then the boss.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we meet at nine o'clock in the meeting room, I bring coffee, and we greet the team first and then the boss. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r> <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
A new colleague is at your company and so far only knows their own department. You would like to show them the other departments.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
Where? (reception, office)
Which department first? (purchasing, sales)

q.en: Hi Mark! You're new at the company and have only seen your own department so far. Shall we visit the other departments together?

a.en:
I like that a lot. I'd like to get to know the colleagues because I don't know anyone yet.
I have a suggestion: We start tomorrow at ten o'clock.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because all the departments have a meeting at ten o'clock tomorrow.
We could do it like this: we start at eleven o'clock.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we meet at the reception?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
One idea would be that we go to Sales first and then to Purchasing.
What do you think about that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we meet tomorrow at eleven o'clock at the reception and go to Sales first and then to Purchasing. Thanks for your help, Anna! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You are new at the company. On Friday you are supposed to introduce yourself to the team. A colleague helps you practice.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
Where? (office, break room)
What to say? (name, department, hobby)

q.en: Hi Alex! On Friday I'm supposed to introduce myself to the team. I have never done that in German. Can you <g>help me</g>?

a.en:
Gladly, I'll do that.
My suggestion would be that we practice tomorrow at twelve o'clock.
Are you okay with that?

q1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. I'd rather practice twice.
How about if we practice today and tomorrow at twelve o'clock?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
Why don't we just practice in the break room?

q2.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
I would suggest that I say my name, my department and my hobby.
What do you think about that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we practice today and tomorrow at twelve o'clock in the break room, and you say your name, your department and your hobby. Then the team will surely <g>like</g> your introduction! Good luck on Friday! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
The company is getting a new website. You and a colleague would like to take a photo of the whole team.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
Where? (entrance, garden)
Who stands where? (boss, new colleagues)

q.en: Hi Julia! We need a new team photo for the website. I have already asked all the colleagues, and everyone is taking part. Shall we plan it together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's take the photo on Tuesday at ten o'clock.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we take the photo in front of the entrance?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
We could do it like this: the boss stands in the middle and everyone else stands around her.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
That sounds good, but maybe we should also think about the new colleagues.
I suggest that the new colleagues stand right next to the boss.
How do you like that?

a2.en: <r>Agreed, that works well.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we meet on Tuesday at ten o'clock in front of the entrance. The boss stands in the middle, the new colleagues stand next to her, and everyone smiles! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You want to move soon because your flat is too small. You have found a new flat and would like to see it. A friend comes along.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
How do we get there? (bus, car)
What do we ask? (lift, rent)

q.en: Hi Alex! I want to move soon because my flat is too small. I <g>have found</g> an ad on the internet. Will you come along to the viewing?

a.en:
Of course, gladly.
We could go to the viewing on Saturday at eleven o'clock.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we go by car?

a1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. There are hardly any parking spaces in the city centre on Saturdays.
My suggestion would be that we take the bus.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that we ask the landlord about the lift and the rent.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> on Saturday we take the bus to the viewing at eleven o'clock and ask the landlord about the lift and the rent. I'm already looking forward to your new flat, Anna! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
A friend is coming to visit at the weekend and will sleep in your guest room. You and your flatmate would like to prepare the room.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
Where do we put the bed? (window, wall)
Where do we hang the picture? (bed, door)

q.en: Hi David! My friend is coming to visit on Saturday and will sleep in our guest room. We still have to prepare the room. Can you help me?

a.en:
Sure, no problem.
How about if we start on Friday evening?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we put the bed by the window.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
To be honest, I'm not so convinced. It's often cold by the window at night.
My suggestion would be that we put the bed against the wall.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
We could hang the big picture above the bed.
How do you like that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we start on Friday evening, put the bed against the wall and hang the big picture above the bed. Your friend will surely sleep well! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
Your room is too dark. You would like to renovate it and make it bright and cosy. A friend helps you.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
Which colour? (white, yellow)
Who buys what? (paint, brushes)

q.en: Hi Max! I want to renovate my room <g>because</g> it is too dark. It should become bright and cosy. Will you help me?

a.en:
No problem, I'm happy to help you.
My suggestion would be that we start on Saturday at ten o'clock.
What do you think of that?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
We could paint the room white.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
In principle I'm in favour, but I'm not sure about white. I prefer yellow because it is cosier.
We could do it like this: we take a light yellow.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
What do you think about it if I buy the paint and you bring the brushes?

a2.en: <r>Sounds great, let's do it that way.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we start on Saturday at ten o'clock and paint the room light yellow. You buy the paint, and I bring the brushes. Then your room will soon be bright and cosy! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and your flatmate have just moved into the flat share. You would like to throw a housewarming party.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (Saturday, time)
Whom do we invite? (neighbours, friends)
Who brings what? (drinks, salad)

q.en: Hi Mark! We've been living in the flat share for two weeks now. Shall we have a housewarming party?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
I have a suggestion: we celebrate on Saturday at seven o'clock.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just invite all the neighbours and a few friends?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that I buy the drinks.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
That's okay for me, but we'd still have to clarify who is making the food.
I would suggest that I make a big salad.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We celebrate on Saturday at seven o'clock and invite all the neighbours and a few friends. I buy the drinks, and you make the salad. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
A colleague is leaving your company soon. You and a colleague would like to buy him a leaving present.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we give him? (book, voucher)
When do we buy the present? (day, time)
Who hands it over? (boss, us)

q.en: Hi Max! Our colleague is leaving the company next week. We want to buy him a present. Can you help me?

a.en:
Gladly, I'll do that.
How about if we give him a voucher?

q1.en:
To be honest, I'm not so convinced. He loves reading.
I would suggest that we give him a book.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
We could buy the book on Friday during the lunch break.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
One idea would be that the boss gives him the present.
How do you like that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We buy a book on Friday during the lunch break, and the boss gives it to him. I'll ask her today. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and a friend would like to do a course together in your free time. The city has many leisure activities on offer.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Which course? (dancing, painting)
When? (day, time)
How do we sign up? (internet, phone)

q.en: Hi Alex! The city has lots of new leisure activities. I'd like to do a course. Will you join me?

a.en:
Of course, gladly. I think that a course is a good idea.
We could do a dance course.
How do you like that?

q1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. I think that I can't dance well.
How about if we do a painting course?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we go on Wednesday evening.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
What do you think about it if we sign up on the internet?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We do a painting course on Wednesday evening and sign up on the internet today. I hope <g>that</g> there are still places! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and a friend wanted to study together for the German test. Unfortunately you had to cancel the meeting. Now you would like to find a new date.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
Where? (library, at home)
What do we study? (words, grammar)

q.en: Hi David! We <g>wanted</g> to study together yesterday, but I <g>had to</g> work longer. Can we plan the study session again?

a.en:
That's not a problem.
How about if we study on Saturday at ten o'clock?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just study in the library?

a1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the library is closed at the weekend.
We could do it like this: we study at my place.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that we revise the grammar first.
How do you like that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We study on Saturday at ten o'clock at my place and revise the grammar first. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and a friend would like to get fitter. You would like to do a trial session at the gym together.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
What do we take with us? (sportswear, water)
What do we ask at the gym? (price, membership)

q.en: Hi Max! I'd like to do more for my fitness after work. Do you fancy a trial session at the gym?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
Let's go on Wednesday after work.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the gym is closed on Wednesdays.
We could do it like this: we go on Thursday.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I suggest that we take sportswear, water and a towel.
How do you like that?

q2.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
Why don't we just ask at the gym about the price of the membership?

a2.en: <r>Sounds great, let's do it that way.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We go to the trial session on Thursday after work, take sportswear, water and a towel and ask about the price of the membership. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
You are clearing out your wardrobe and would like to donate old clothes. A friend helps you.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we donate? (coat, jumper)
Where do we take the clothes? (clothing bank, container)
When? (day, time)

q.en: Hi Max! My wardrobe is full. I'd like to donate old clothes. Can you <g>help me</g>?

a.en:
Sure, no problem.
I have a suggestion: we start with the coat and the hats.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we take everything to the clothing bank?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we go there on Friday after work.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
That's okay for me, but we'd still have to clarify what about the jumpers. They don't fit me any more.
We could take the jumpers too.
What do you think about that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We take the coat, the hats and the jumpers to the clothing bank on Friday after work. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
A colleague's birthday is coming up. You and a friend would like to give her an item of clothing.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we give her? (scarf, blouse)
Which size? (S, M, L)
Where do we buy it? (department store, internet)

q.en: Hi Mark! Our colleague has her birthday next week. I'd like to give her an item of clothing. Can you help me?

a.en:
Of course, gladly.
How about if we buy her a warm scarf?

q1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. She never wears scarves.
I would suggest that we buy her a blue blouse.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
We could take size M. She is as tall as you.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Sounds great, let's do it that way.
What do you think about it if we buy the blouse in the department store?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We buy her a blue blouse in size M in the department store. <r>Good, then that's settled.</r> <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and a friend are invited to a fancy-dress party. You would like to dress up in a funny way.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What kind of costume? (pirate, clown)
Which colours and patterns? (colourful, striped, checked)
Where and when do we buy the things? (department store, Friday)

q.en: Hi Alex! There's a fancy-dress party on Saturday. We want to dress up in a funny way. Shall we choose a costume together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
We could be two pirates.
How do you like that?

q1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we both wear a striped shirt and red trousers.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because I don't have any red trousers.
How about if we buy red trousers in the department store?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just go on Friday after work?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We are two pirates and both wear a striped shirt and red trousers. We buy the things in the department store on Friday after work. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
You and a friend are going on a trip to the lake at the weekend. You would like to think about what to wear and take with you.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (Saturday, time)
What do we wear? (swimwear, flip-flops)
What else do we take? (sun cream, towel)

q.en: Hi Max! On Saturday we're going to the lake together. We still have to think about what to wear and take with us. Do you have time?

a.en:
Yes, gladly.
I have a suggestion: we set off at nine o'clock.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we wear swimwear and flip-flops.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
That could work if we also take a warm jacket.
We could also take sun cream and towels.
How do you like that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
How about if we I bring the towels?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We set off on Saturday at nine o'clock, wear swimwear and flip-flops and take a warm jacket and sun cream. You bring the towels. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You take the bus to work every day and would rather buy a bike. A friend comes with you.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Where do we buy the bike? (shop, internet)
When do we go? (day, time)
How much may we spend? (price)

q.en: Hi Alex! I take the bus to work every day. I'd rather buy a bike. Will you come with me?

a.en:
Of course, gladly.
We could go to the bike shop. If it is too expensive, we'll look on the internet.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we go on Saturday at ten o'clock?

a1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the shop doesn't open until eleven o'clock on Saturdays.
We could do it like this: we go at eleven o'clock.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that we spend two hundred euros at most.
How do you like that?

a2.en: <r>Agreed, that works well.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We go to the bike shop on Saturday at eleven o'clock and spend two hundred euros at most. <g>If</g> the bike is too expensive, we'll look on the internet. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and a colleague have an important appointment in the city tomorrow. It is supposed to rain. You would like to share a taxi.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When do we order the taxi? (time)
Where do we get in? (office, bus stop)
Who pays? (half each, the company)

q.en: Hi Max! Tomorrow we have an important appointment in the city. It's supposed to rain all day. Shall we take a taxi together?

a.en:
I like that a lot. I don't want to be late because the appointment is so important.
I have a suggestion: we order the taxi for half past seven.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because there is a lot of traffic in the morning.
We could do it like this: we order the taxi for seven o'clock.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we get in in front of the office?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that everyone pays half.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We order the taxi for seven o'clock, get in in front of the office and both pay half. Then we'll arrive on time for the appointment! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and a colleague would like to cycle to work together from next week.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Which route? (park, main road)
When do we set off? (time)
Where do we meet? (in front of the house, bus stop)

q.en: Hi Alex! I'd like to cycle to work from next week. Shall we cycle together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
I have a suggestion: we take the route through the park. It is quieter than the main road.
What do you think?

q1.en:
To be honest, I'm not so convinced. The route through the park is longer than the main road.
We could do it like this: we ride through the park in the morning and along the main road in the evening.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we set off at half past seven.
How do you like that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we meet in front of my house?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We meet at half past seven in front of your house, ride through the park in the morning and along the main road in the evening. After all, the bike is <g>more environmentally friendly than</g> the car! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and a colleague are going to a training course in Munich next week. You would like to buy the tickets together.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Which connection? (train, long-distance bus)
When do we travel? (outward, return)
Where do we buy the tickets? (internet, ticket counter)

q.en: Hi Max! Next week we're going to a training course in Munich together. We still have to buy the tickets. Do you have a moment?

a.en:
Yes, gladly.
I have a suggestion: we take the ICE. It is the fastest.
What do you think?

q1.en:
To be honest, I'm not so convinced. The ICE is the most expensive.
We could do it like this: we take the long-distance bus. It is the cheapest.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we travel there early on Monday and back on Wednesday evening.
How do you like that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just buy the tickets on the internet?

a2.en: <r>Sounds great, let's do it that way.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We take the long-distance bus, going there early on Monday and coming back on Wednesday evening, and buy the tickets on the internet today. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
Your parents live in another country. You and your brother / sister would like to have a video call with them.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
Who calls? (you, me)
What do we show? (photos, flat)

q.en: Hi Alex! Our parents live in another country. We <g>want to</g> have a video call with them. Will you plan it with me?

a.en:
Sure, no problem.
How about if we call on Sunday at seven o'clock?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that I call our parents.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
We could show photos of our flat. Then Mum and Dad can see the flat.
How do you like that?

q2.en:
That's okay for me, but we'd still have to clarify how long we'll talk.
How about if we talk on the phone for an hour?

a2.en: <r>Perfect, let's do it that way.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We talk on Sunday at seven o'clock for an hour, you call Mum and Dad, and we show photos of our flat. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
New neighbours have recently immigrated to Germany. You and a friend would like to invite them to a coffee get-together.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
Where? (café, garden)
How long? (one hour, two hours)

q.en: Hi Max! Our new neighbours immigrated to Germany <g>three months ago</g>. They don't know many people yet. Shall we invite them to a coffee get-together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
I have a suggestion: we invite them on Friday after work.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the neighbours work until eight o'clock on Fridays.
We could do it like this: we invite them on Saturday at three o'clock.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we invite them to the café on the corner?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that we stay for two hours.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We invite the neighbours to the café on the corner on Saturday at three o'clock and stay for two hours. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
Your parents' wedding anniversary is coming up. You and your brother / sister would like to give them a photo album.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What goes into the album? (childhood photos, holiday pictures)
When do we start? (day, time)
Who buys the album? (you, me)

q.en: Hi Alex! Our parents' wedding anniversary is coming up, and we want to give them a photo album. <g>Whenever</g> we had holidays, Dad always took lots of photos. Will you help me?

a.en:
Sure, no problem.
We could start with the childhood photos. When I was five, we had a great holiday at the sea.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just start on Friday?

a1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the photos won't be ready until Saturday.
We could do it like this: we start on Saturday.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that I buy the album.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We start on Saturday with the childhood photos and the holiday pictures, and you buy the album. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
Your grandparents are about to celebrate their golden wedding anniversary. You and your cousin would like to give a short speech.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When do we write the speech? (day, time)
What do we talk about? (family, life, funny story)
Who speaks first? (you, me)

q.en: Hi Max! Our grandparents are about to celebrate their golden wedding anniversary. We want to give a short speech. Will you plan it with me?

a.en:
Of course, gladly.
How about if we write it together on Saturday?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
We could talk about their family and their life.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
Actually yes, but wouldn't it be better if we also told a funny story?
I have a suggestion: we tell the story of their first dance.
How do you like that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that you speak first.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>Agreed, that works well.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We write the speech together on Saturday, talk about the family, the grandparents' life and their first dance, and I speak first. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
You would like to go on a trip to an old castle on Saturday. A friend comes along.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
How do we get there? (train, car)
When do we set off? (time)
What do we do there? (hiking trail, visit the castle)

q.en: Hi David! On Saturday I'd like to go on a trip to the old castle. Will you come along?

a.en:
Of course, gladly.
We could go by train. If we take the train, we don't have to park.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just set off at eight o'clock?

a1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the first train on Saturdays doesn't leave until half past eight.
We could do it like this: we leave at half past eight.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that we take the hiking trail to the castle first. When we are at the top, we'll have something to eat.
What do you think about that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We take the train on Saturday at half past eight, go along the hiking trail to the castle first and have something to eat at the top. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
A friend from abroad is visiting you on Saturday. You and a friend would like to plan the programme for the day.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we show first? (church, castle)
When and where do we eat? (lunchtime, café)
Who picks up the guest? (station)

q.en: Hi Max! On Saturday a friend from abroad is visiting us. We still have to plan the programme for the day. Do you have any ideas?

a.en:
Sure, no problem.
We could show him the church first and then the castle. This castle is really beautiful.
How do you like that?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just eat at one o'clock in the restaurant on the market square?

a1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because this restaurant is always full at lunchtime.
We could do it like this: we eat at two o'clock in the café by the castle.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that you pick him up at the station.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We show him the church and the castle first, eat at two o'clock in the café by the castle, and I pick him up at the station. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
Last Saturday was your company's outing. You and a colleague would like to write a short report for the company newspaper.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When do we write the report? (day, time)
What do we write about? (weather, food, games)
Which photos do we use? (group photo, food)

q.en: Hi Alex! Last Saturday we <g>had</g> the company outing. The boss would like a short report for the company newspaper. Will you write it with me?

a.en:
Sure, no problem.
How about if we write it tomorrow during the lunch break?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we write about the weather and the food.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
Actually yes, but wouldn't it be better if we also wrote about the games?
I have a suggestion: we write: the weather was sunny and everyone had a lot of fun.
How do you like that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
How about if we use the group photo and a photo of the food?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We write tomorrow during the lunch break about the weather, the food and the games and use the group photo and a photo of the food. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and a friend would like to go away at the weekend and stay overnight in a youth hostel. You would like to book the room.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
How many nights? (one, two)
Which room? (double room, dormitory)
Who books? (you, me)

q.en: Hi Max! At the weekend we want to go away together. I'd like to stay overnight in a youth hostel. Shall we book the room together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
I have a suggestion: we stay two nights.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just take a double room?

a1.en:
In principle I'm in favour, but I'm not sure about a double room. It's often very cramped.
We could do it like this: we take a four-bed room.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that I book the room on the internet this evening.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We stay two nights in a four-bed room, and you book it on the internet this evening. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
A friend is coming to Berlin to visit you. You and a friend would like to describe the way to your flat.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
By which means of transport? (underground, bus)
Which way from the stop? (bridge, park)
Who picks up the guest? (you, me)

q.en: Hi Alex! Tomorrow our friend from Hamburg is coming <g>to Berlin</g>. He doesn't know the city yet. Shall we write him the directions to our flat together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
I have a suggestion: he takes the underground to Alexanderplatz.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the underground isn't running there at the moment.
We could do it like this: he takes the bus.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that he goes over the bridge and then straight on to our house.
How do you like that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that I pick him up at the stop.
What do you think about that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> He takes the bus to Alexanderplatz, goes over the bridge and then straight on to our house, and you pick him up at the stop. I'll write him the directions today. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You are a trainer in a company. New apprentices start on Monday. You and a colleague would like to plan the first day.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When does the day start? (time)
Where do we meet the apprentices? (entrance, canteen)
Where do we go first? (workshop, vocational school)

q.en: Hi Max! On Monday three new apprentices start with us. We still have to plan the first day. Do you have a moment?

a.en:
Yes, gladly.
I have a suggestion: we start at nine o'clock.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we meet the apprentices at the entrance?

a1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the entrance doesn't open until half past nine on Mondays.
We could do it like this: we meet them in the canteen.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that we go with them to the workshop first and then to the vocational school.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We start at nine o'clock, meet the apprentices in the canteen and go with them to the workshop first and then to the vocational school. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
A colleague is coming to your place for dinner on Saturday. She is a big fan of Italian food. You and your flatmate would like to plan the menu.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we cook? (pasta, pizza)
What is there for dessert? (ice cream, tiramisu)
Who does the shopping? (you, me)

q.en: Hi Mark! On Saturday our colleague is coming for dinner. She is <g>a big fan</g> of Italian food. Shall we plan the menu together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
We could cook lasagne. It is a typical dish from Italy.
How do you like that?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because our colleague doesn't eat meat.
We could do it like this: we cook pasta with a light sauce.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we make tiramisu for dessert.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that you do the shopping tomorrow.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We cook pasta with a light sauce and make tiramisu for dessert, and I do the shopping tomorrow. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
There is a new exhibition nearby. You and a friend would like to visit it at the weekend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
How do we get there? (on foot, bus)
Whom else do we ask? (colleagues, friends)

q.en: Hi David! There's a new exhibition nearby. I'd like to visit it at the weekend. Will you come along?

a.en:
Of course, gladly.
We could go on Saturday at eleven o'clock.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just go on foot?

a1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. The way is quite far.
My suggestion would be that we take the bus.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that we also ask a few colleagues.
What do you think about that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We take the bus to the exhibition on Saturday at eleven o'clock and also ask a few colleagues. I'll write to them today. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
Your child has received a good school report. You and your partner would like to celebrate with a small party.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When do we celebrate? (day, time)
What do we do? (bake a cake, games)
What present does the child get? (book, football)

q.en: Hi Max! Our son <g>has got</g> a very good school report. We'd like to celebrate that with a small party. Shall we plan it together?

a.en:
I like that a lot. He studied so hard this term.
I have a suggestion: we celebrate on Saturday at three o'clock.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. The grandparents won't arrive until four o'clock.
We could do it like this: we celebrate at five o'clock.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we bake a cake together?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that he gets a new book.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We celebrate on Saturday at five o'clock, bake a cake together, and he gets a new book. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
You are a parent representative. The school will soon hold a school fair. You and another parent representative would like to prepare it.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When is the fair? (Saturday, time)
Where do we celebrate? (schoolyard, gym)
Who brings what? (cake, drinks)

q.en: Hi David! The children are already <g>looking forward to</g> the school fair. We still have to prepare it. Shall we plan it together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
I have a suggestion: we celebrate on Saturday at ten o'clock.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just celebrate in the schoolyard?

a1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because a football tournament is taking place in the schoolyard on Saturday.
We could do it like this: we celebrate in the gym.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that I think of the drinks and you bring the cake.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We celebrate on Saturday at ten o'clock in the gym, I bring the cake, and you <g>think of</g> the drinks. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
Your daughter will soon move to a secondary school. You and your partner would like to visit a school on its open day.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When do we go? (day, time)
What do we ask? (grades, breaks, teachers)
Who comes along? (daughter, grandparents)

q.en: Hi Alex! Our daughter is changing to a new school next year. On Saturday it's the open day. Shall we go?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
We could go there at ten o'clock.
How do you like that?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we ask about the grades and the breaks.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
That could work if we also add a question about school-leaving qualifications.
We could also take our daughter with us.
How do you like that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
Why don't we just check on the internet beforehand when the tour starts?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We go there on Saturday at ten o'clock, ask about the grades, the breaks and the school-leaving qualification, take our daughter with us and check beforehand on the internet when the tour starts. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
Your son only got a pass mark in the maths test. You and your partner would like to organise tutoring for him.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Who gives the tutoring? (student, teacher)
When is the tutoring? (day, time)
Where? (at home, at school)

q.en: Hi Max! Our son only got a pass mark in the maths test. He needs tutoring. Shall we organise it together?

a.en:
That's not a problem.
We could ask a student.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. Students often have little time.
I would suggest that the class teacher recommends someone.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
Why don't we just start on Tuesdays and Thursdays at four o'clock?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I suggest that the tutoring takes place at our home.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> The class teacher recommends someone, and the tutoring is on Tuesdays and Thursdays at four o'clock at our home. I'll talk to the class teacher tomorrow. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
The neighbours above you play loud music every evening. You and another neighbour would like to write a complaint.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we write? (times, noise)
Who writes the letter? (you, me)
When do we take it there? (day, time)

q.en: Hi Max! The neighbours above us play loud music every evening. The noise disturbs me, <g>so</g> I'd like to write a complaint. Will you write it with me?

a.en:
Sure, no problem. The noise disturbs me too, so I'm happy to join in.
I have a suggestion: we write down the times exactly.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that I write the letter.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
We could take the letter to the property management tomorrow morning.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the property management only opens at ten o'clock.
We could do it like this: we take it there at ten o'clock.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>Agreed, that works well.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We write down the times exactly, you write the letter, and we take it to the property management tomorrow at ten o'clock. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and a friend forgot the birthday of a mutual friend. You would like to apologise to her.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When do we visit her? (this evening, tomorrow)
What do we give her? (flowers, cake)
What do we say? (apology, explanation)

q.en: Hi Alex! Yesterday we forgot our friend's birthday. We <g>should</g> apologise to her. Will you plan it with me?

a.en:
Of course, gladly.
How about if we visit her this evening?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because she is working this evening.
We could do it like this: we visit her tomorrow after work.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that. I would like to give her something special.
I would suggest that we give her flowers.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I suggest that we honestly say: We are very sorry.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We visit her tomorrow after work, give her flowers and honestly say: We are very sorry. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and a colleague are giving a presentation together next week. You would like to divide up the work.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Who does what? (slides, text, talk)
When are we finished? (day)
When do we practise? (day, time)

q.en: Hi Max! Next week we're giving a presentation together. We still have to divide up the work. Will you plan it with me?

a.en:
Sure, no problem.
I have a suggestion: you make the slides, and I prepare the talk.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. I prefer writing the text.
How about if we I write the text and you make the slides?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that we are finished by Friday.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just practise together on Monday at ten o'clock?

a2.en: <r>Sounds great, let's do it that way.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> You make the slides, I write the text and prepare the talk, we are finished by Friday and practise together on Monday at ten o'clock. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and a friend would like to go on holiday together in summer. You have different wishes and would like to reach an agreement.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Where do we go? (mountains, sea, lake)
How long do we stay? (one week, ten days)
Who plans what? (accommodation, journey)

q.en: Hi David! We want to go on holiday together in summer. I'd like to go to the sea. Shall we choose the destination together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
I have a suggestion: we go to the mountains.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. I was already in the mountains last year.
How about if we go to a lake in the mountains?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we stay ten days.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that I look for the accommodation and you plan the journey.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We go to a lake in the mountains and stay ten days. I plan the journey, and you look for the accommodation. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
You and a friend would like to have a film night at home on Friday evening.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we watch? (comedy, thriller)
When do we start? (time)
What do we eat with it? (popcorn, pizza)

q.en: Hi David! On Friday I'd like to have a film night. Shall we plan it together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
We could watch the new thriller.
How do you like that?

q1.en:
To be honest, I'm not so convinced. I don't like thrillers.
I would suggest that we watch the funny comedy.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
How about if we start at eight o'clock?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I suggest that we make popcorn to go with it.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We watch the funny comedy, start at eight o'clock and make popcorn to go with it. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
The washing machine in your flat share is broken but still under warranty. You and a flatmate would like to call customer service.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When do we call? (today, tomorrow)
What do we say? (problem, warranty)
Who waits for the technician? (you, me)

q.en: Hi Mark! <g>The broken washing machine</g> doesn't work at all any more. But it's still under warranty. Shall we call customer service?

a.en:
That's not a problem.
How about if we call this evening?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because customer service can't be reached in the evening.
We could do it like this: we call tomorrow morning.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we explain the problem and ask for the next free appointment.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that you wait at home for the technician.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We call tomorrow morning, explain the problem and ask for the next free appointment, and I wait at home for the technician. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
Your phone is almost full because you have taken lots of photos. You and a friend would like to back up the photos.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Where do we store the photos? (cloud, hard drive)
When do we do it? (day, time)
Who installs the program? (you, me)

q.en: Hi Max! My phone is almost full. I'd like to back up my photos. Can you help me?

a.en:
Of course, gladly.
We could use a free cloud.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. I don't have a good internet connection.
How about if we buy an external hard drive?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
Why don't we just start on Sunday?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that you install the program.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We buy an external hard drive, start on Sunday, and I install the program. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
Your grandma's birthday is coming up. You and your brother / sister would like to film a short video for her.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When do we film? (day, time)
Where do we film? (garden, living room)
Who says what? (you, me, both)

q.en: Hi Max! Our grandma's birthday is coming up. I'd like to film a short video for her. Will you join in?

a.en:
Of course, gladly.
How about if we film on Saturday evening?

q.en: Hi Max! Our son <g>is turning</g> sixteen soon. He wants to <g>become</g> a baker. Shall we organise a work placement for him?

I like that a lot.

task.en:
You have two apprenticeship places to choose from and can't decide. You and a friend would like to prepare the decision.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we write down? (advantages, disadvantages)
When do we meet? (day, time)
Whom else do we ask? (parents, teacher)

q.en: Hi Mia! I have two apprenticeship places and can't decide. <g>Could</g> you help me?

a.en:
Sure, no problem.
I have a suggestion: we write down all the advantages and disadvantages. You shouldn't forget anything.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we meet tomorrow at six o'clock?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we also ask your parents.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Actually yes, but wouldn't it be better if we decided on our own first?
I would like to make a suggestion: we only ask the parents when the list is finished.
How do you like that?

a2.en: <r>Agreed, that works well.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We write down all the advantages and disadvantages, meet tomorrow at six o'clock and only ask your parents when the list is finished. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You are applying for an apprenticeship and need a reference from your former boss. You and a friend would like to plan the request.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
How do we ask? (email, phone)
What do we say? (application deadline, reason)
When do we ask? (today, tomorrow)

q.en: Hi Julia! I'm applying for an apprenticeship. I still need a reference from my former boss. I hope <g>that</g> he <g>helps</g> me. Will you plan it with me?

What do you think?

q1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. I think that he rarely reads emails.
How about if we call him?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that you tell him the application deadline.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just call first thing tomorrow morning?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We call him tomorrow morning, and you tell him the application deadline. I hope <g>that</g> he <g>says</g> yes! <r>See you then!</r>
