How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We set off at half past seven, meet at the bakery and send each other a message in the evening. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You are new at the company and still need the key to your office. A colleague would like to help you.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Where? (reception, canteen)
When? (time)
What else? (coffee, show the office)

q.en: Hello! I'm Anna and new here. I still need the key to my office. Can you <g>help me</g>?

a.en:
Sure, no problem. I'm happy to help you.
We could go to the reception first and get the key.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
How about if we go there right away?

a1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the reception doesn't open until nine o'clock.
We could do it like this: we have a coffee in the canteen until then.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Okay, I understand. A coffee will definitely taste good to me now.
I would suggest that you show me the office afterwards.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Agreed, that works well.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We first have a coffee in the canteen, at nine o'clock we get the key, and afterwards I'll show <g>you</g> the office. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
A new colleague starts next week. You and a colleague would like to organise a welcome party for her together.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
Where? (canteen, office)
Who brings what? (cake, drinks)

q.en: Hi Mark! Next week a new colleague starts. Shall we organise a welcome party for her together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
I have a suggestion: we celebrate on Friday afternoon.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because many colleagues leave early on Fridays.
We could do it like this: we celebrate as early as two o'clock.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just celebrate in the canteen?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that you bring the drinks and I bake a cake.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We celebrate on Friday at two o'clock in the canteen, I bring the drinks, and you bake a cake. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
Your friend is moving at the weekend. You would like to help him with the move.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
What do we bring? (van, boxes)
Who carries what? (wardrobe, furniture)

q.en: Hi Mark! I've <g>heard</g> that you're moving at the weekend. Can I help you?

a.en:
Yes, gladly.
How about if we start on Saturday morning?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we hire a van.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because vans are often already booked out on Saturdays. My brother has often helped me.
We could do it like this: we ask my brother, he has a van.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we carry the wardrobe together.
How do you like that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We start on Saturday morning, my brother brings the van, and we carry the wardrobe together. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and a flatmate have just moved into a new flat share. You would like to set up the furniture in the living room together.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Where do we put the sofa? (wall, window)
Where should the table stand? (in front of the sofa, next to the window)
Where does the shelf go? (corner, wall)

q.en: Hi Alex! We still have to set up the furniture in the living room. Do you have time?

a.en:
Sure, no problem.
We could put the sofa against the wall.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That's okay for me, but we'd still have to clarify where the table goes.
I have a suggestion: the table stands in front of the sofa.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because then the door won't open.
We could do it like this: we put the table next to the window.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that we put the shelf in the corner.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We put the sofa against the wall, the table next to the window and the shelf in the corner. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
You and your flatmate would like to sell old furniture. Beforehand you have to tidy up the room and take photos.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When do we tidy up? (Friday, Saturday)
What price do we ask? (fair, cheap)
Who writes the classified ad? (you, me)

q.en: Hi Mia! We should sell the old sofa and the shelf. Do you feel like planning it together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
How about if we tidy up the room on Saturday?

q1.en:
That's okay for me, but we'd still have to clarify when we take the photos. Photos are better in the morning because the light is good then.
I have a suggestion: we tidy up as early as Friday evening.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well. The price has to be low because the sofa is already old.
My suggestion would be that we ask fifty euros.
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that I write the classified ad.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We tidy up on Friday evening, take the photos on Saturday morning and ask fifty euros for the sofa, and you write the classified ad. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and your flatmate have been arguing about the housework a lot lately. You would like to draw up a cleaning rota.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Who does what? (kitchen, bathroom)
How often do we swap? (every week, every month)
Who takes out the rubbish? (you, me, taking turns)

q.en: Hi Nina! We've been arguing about the housework a lot lately. Shall we make a cleaning rota?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
We could share out the tasks: I clean the bathroom.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that I take over the kitchen.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Actually yes, but wouldn't it be better if we swapped every week?
My suggestion would be that we swap every Sunday.
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
Why don't we just take out the rubbish in turns?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> I clean the bathroom, you the kitchen, we swap every Sunday and take out the rubbish in turns. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and a friend would like to join a sports club together. There will also be a competition soon.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Which sport? (volleyball, table tennis)
When is the training? (Wednesday, time)
Do we go to the competition? (yes, no)

q.en: Hi Julia! I've heard <g>that</g> the sports club is looking for new members. Shall we go there together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
We could play volleyball together.
How do you like that?

q1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. I think that the volleyball group is already full.
How about if we try table tennis first?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that we go to the training on Wednesday.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
We could afterwards go to the team's competition.
What do you think about that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We try table tennis, go to the training on Wednesday and then to the competition. I hope <g>that</g> we <g>like</g> it! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
Unfortunately you had to cancel your last meeting with a friend. Now you would like to find a new date.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
What do we do? (cinema, football)
Who writes it in the calendar? (you, me)

q.en: Hi Alex! I'm sorry, I <g>had to</g> cancel our meeting last week. Shall we find a new date?

a.en:
That's not a problem.
I have a suggestion: we meet on Saturday at five o'clock.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just go to the cinema?

a1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. Last week we wanted to play football.
My suggestion would be that we play football first and then go to the cinema.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that. Last time we both couldn't, now it works.
I would suggest that I put the date in the calendar right away.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Agreed, that works well.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We meet on Saturday at five o'clock, play football first and then go to the cinema, and you put the date in the calendar. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and a friend had a lot of stress this week. You would like to go hiking together at the weekend to relax.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
Where to? (lake, mountain)
What do we take with us? (food, drinks)

q.en: Hi Mark! This week was pretty stressful. Shall we go hiking together at the weekend?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
How about if we set off on Saturday morning?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the bus to the hiking trail doesn't leave until ten o'clock on Saturdays.
We could do it like this: we set off at ten o'clock.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I suggest that we hike to the lake in the forest.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that we take something to eat and drink with us.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We set off on Saturday at ten o'clock, hike to the lake in the forest and take something to eat and drink with us. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
You and a friend are invited to a wedding together. You would like to think about what to wear.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Which clothes? (dress, trousers)
Who lends what to whom? (scarf, shoes)
When do we get dressed? (time)

q.en: Hi Julia! On Saturday we're invited to the wedding. I don't have an outfit yet. Can you <g>help me</g>?

a.en:
Sure, no problem.
We could wear your blue dress.
What do you think?

q1.en:
To be honest, I'm not so convinced. I don't like the dress so much any more.
I would suggest that I wear the black trousers with a blouse.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that you borrow my scarf. It has belonged to me for a long time.
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we meet at my place at six o'clock?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> You wear the black trousers with a blouse, I lend you my scarf, and we meet at your place at six o'clock. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You need new clothes for autumn. A friend would like to go shopping with you.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When do we go? (day, time)
What do we look for? (jumper, shirt)
Where do we meet? (station, department store)

q.en: Hi Alex! I need new clothes for autumn. Will you go shopping with me?

a.en:
Of course, gladly.
How about if we go into town on Saturday?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the shops are very busy on Saturdays.
We could do it like this: we go as early as Friday afternoon.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we look for a warm jumper first and then a new shirt.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we meet at the station.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We go into town on Friday afternoon, meet at the station and look for a warm jumper first and then a new shirt. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You have great news from your holiday and would like to meet a friend to tell her about it.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
Where? (at my place, café)
What do we bring? (photos, cake)

q.en: Hi Anna! I was on holiday and took great photos. Shall we meet for a coffee?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
How about if we meet on Tuesday?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because I already have an appointment on Tuesday.
We could do it like this: we meet on Wednesday. Then I'll show you the photos.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just have coffee at my place?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that I bring you a cake.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We meet on Wednesday at my place, you show me the photos, and you bring a cake. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
Your friend still needs a shirt for a party. You would like to go to the department store together.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
Where do we meet? (in front of the department store, station)
Which colour and pattern? (dark, striped)

q.en: Hi Mark! You still need a shirt for the party. Shall we go to the department store?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
I have a suggestion: we go there tomorrow afternoon.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we meet in front of the department store at three o'clock?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
My suggestion would be that I take a dark shirt. It suits any party.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Actually yes, but wouldn't it be better if you took a striped shirt?
I have a suggestion: we both have a look, and then you decide.
How do you like that?

a2.en: <r>Agreed, that works well.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We meet tomorrow at three o'clock in front of the department store, look for a dark and a striped shirt, and I decide then. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and a colleague are invited to the company anniversary. You would like to think about what to wear for this festive occasion.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Which clothes? (dress, suit)
How comfortable should it be? (loose, tight)
What else? (jewellery, shoes)

q.en: Hi Nina! On Friday it's the company anniversary. Shall we plan our clothes for it together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
We could wear elegant dresses.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. I'd also like to wear comfortable shoes.
How about if we take loose dresses? They are more comfortable.

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we also wear some jewellery with it.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
That's okay for me, but we'd still have to clarify which jewellery we take.
I would suggest that we both wear a simple necklace.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We wear loose, elegant dresses and both a simple necklace. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
You and a friend would like to go to a concert together on Friday.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Which means of transport? (bike, underground)
When do we set off? (time)
Where do we meet? (stop, in front of the house)

q.en: Hi Mark! On Friday it's the concert. Shall we go there together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
We could go by bike. If we go by bike, we don't need a ticket.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because it's dark on the way back at night.
We could do it like this: we take the underground. When the concert is over, there is still a train.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we set off at seven o'clock?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that we meet at the stop.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We take the underground at seven o'clock and meet at the stop. <g>If</g> we are on time, we'll get good seats! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
Your colleague uses a wheelchair and needs help getting to work. You would like to plan a barrier-free route together.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Which means of transport? (taxi, bus)
When do we set off? (time)
What if we are late? (call the boss)

q.en: Hi Mia! The new underground station isn't barrier-free yet. Shall we plan a good route for you together?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
We could take a taxi in the mornings.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because a taxi every day is too expensive.
We could do it like this: we take the bus. It is barrier-free.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that. Then I won't be stressed because I'll have enough time.
I suggest that we set off at seven o'clock.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we call the boss if we are late.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We take the bus, set off at seven o'clock and call the boss if we are late. Thanks for your help, David! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and your partner would like to visit relatives in another city at the weekend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Which means of transport? (train, car)
When do we set off? (time)
How much may we spend? (price)

q.en: Hi David! At the weekend we want to visit my sister. Will you plan the trip with me?

a.en:
Of course, gladly.
We could go by train. It is faster than the car.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. The train is more expensive than the car.
I would suggest that we go by car.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that. The car is not as expensive as the train.
Why don't we just set off at eight o'clock?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we spend forty euros at most on petrol.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We set off by car on Saturday at eight o'clock and spend forty euros at most on petrol. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You have a job interview next week. A friend would like to help you find the best connection.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Which means of transport? (underground, bus)
When do you set off? (time)
What if something goes wrong? (call)

q.en: Hi Nina! I have a job interview next week. I'm looking for the <g>best</g> connection. Can you help me?

a.en:
Sure, no problem.
I have a suggestion: we take the underground. It is the fastest.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the underground station is the furthest from my flat.
We could do it like this: we take the bus. It stops the closest to my flat.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that you set off an hour earlier.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that I call the company if I'm late.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> You take the bus, set off an hour earlier and call the company if you're late. Good luck, Julia! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
Your cousin's wedding is coming up. You have to invite the relatives abroad.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Whom do we invite? (grandparents, aunts, uncles)
Who may bring someone along? (partner, children)
When do we send the invitations? (day)

q.en: Hi David! Our cousin's wedding is coming up. We <g>have to</g> <g>invite</g> the relatives abroad. Will you help me?

a.en:
Sure, no problem.
I have a suggestion: we invite the grandparents, aunts and uncles first.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because our grandparents can't travel so far.
We could do it like this: we organise a lift for them.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that every guest may bring a companion.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
Why don't we just send the invitations this week already?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We invite the grandparents and relatives first, organise a lift, every guest may bring a companion, and we send the invitations this week. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You haven't been to your home country for five years. You would like to plan a trip there with your partner.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When do we go? (summer, autumn)
What do we sort out beforehand? (passports, leave)
How long do we stay? (two weeks, three weeks)

q.en: Hi Mark! I haven't been to my home country <g>for</g> five years. Shall we plan a trip there?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
How about if we go in summer?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well. Before the trip we still have to renew our passports.
I have a suggestion: we deal with it as early as next week.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the office is closed until Monday.
We could do it like this: we go there on Tuesday.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that we stay for three weeks.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We go in summer, go to the office on Tuesday because of the passports and stay three weeks. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
You would like to organise an evening at which your family remembers old times.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (day, time)
Whom do we invite? (grandparents, parents)
Which questions do we ask? (arrival, childhood)

q.en: Hi Nina! I'd like to organise an evening at which the family remembers old times. <g>When</g> I <g>was</g> little, we often sang together. Will you join in?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
We could start on Sunday at four o'clock.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we invite our grandmother too?

a1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because Grandma doesn't get back until five o'clock on Sunday.
We could do it like this: we only start at five o'clock.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I would suggest that we ask Grandma about her arrival in Germany. When she tells the story, everyone enjoys listening.
How do you see that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We start on Sunday at five o'clock, invite Grandma too and ask her about her arrival in Germany. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You would like to visit your grandparents, who are already retired, with your sister.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When? (Saturday, time)
What do we talk about? (life in the past, neighbourhood)
Do we take the children with us? (yes, no)

q.en: Hi Julia! Shall we visit our grandparents? They'll surely be happy about the grandchildren.

a.en:
I like that a lot.
How about if we go there on Saturday?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because Grandpa always goes to the doctor on Saturdays.
We could do it like this: we go on Sunday.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we ask them about their life in the past.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
We could take the children with us.
How do you like that?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We visit the grandparents on Sunday, ask them about their life in the past and take the children with us. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
You and a friend want to go on a trip at the weekend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Picnic or hike? (park, forest)
What do we do if it rains? (café, museum)
What do we take? (sandwiches, fruit, drinks)

q.en: Hi Julia! At the weekend we want to go on a trip. Do you already have an idea?

a.en:
Yes, I have an idea.
We could have a picnic in the park.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Actually yes, but wouldn't it be better if we checked the weather forecast beforehand?
I have a suggestion: If it rains, we go to the café instead.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we take sandwiches, fruit and drinks.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
We could do it like this: I take an umbrella. If the sun shines, we don't need it.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We have a picnic in the park and take sandwiches, fruit and drinks. If it rains we go to the café, and you bring an umbrella. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You have two ideas for a trip: the zoo or the museum. You would like to decide together with a friend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Zoo or museum? (zoo, museum)
Which museum? (new, old)
When and where do we meet? (time, entrance)

q.en: Hi Mark! Shall we go on a trip on Saturday? I have two ideas: the zoo or the museum.

a.en:
I like that a lot.
We could visit this zoo. It is supposed to be very interesting.
How do you like that?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because this weather forecast predicts a thunderstorm for Saturday.
We could do it like this: we go to the museum instead.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I suggest that we look at this new museum. It is supposed to be very exciting.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
How about if we meet in front of the entrance at eleven o'clock?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We go to the new museum instead and meet in front of the entrance at eleven o'clock. I really like <g>this idea</g>! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You have to plan this year's company outing. Last year the weather wasn't so good.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Where do we go? (park, museum)
What do we do afterwards? (restaurant, bowling)
When is the outing? (day)

q.en: Hi Nina! We have to plan this year's company outing. Do you have an idea?

a.en:
Of course, gladly.
We could go to the park again, like last year.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Hmm, I'm not so sure. Last year the weather was really cold.
How about if we choose an indoor place this time?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that. Last time we had no good plan for the afternoon.
I suggest that we go to the museum and afterwards eat together.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just take the last Friday of the month?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We go to the museum on the last Friday of the month and afterwards eat together. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You would like to go camping at the weekend with a friend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Where do we stay overnight? (lake, forest)
Which activities do we plan? (climbing, campfire)
When do we come back? (Sunday, time)

q.en: Hi Anna! Shall we go camping together at the weekend?

a.en:
I like that a lot.
We could stay overnight by the lake.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because you aren't allowed to camp by the lake.
We could do it like this: we camp in the forest next to the lake.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
I suggest that we go climbing there and have a campfire in the evening.
What do you think about that?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just drive back on Sunday evening?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We camp in the forest next to the lake, go climbing, have a campfire in the evening and drive back on Sunday evening. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
You would like to go to Berlin next month with a friend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Which landmarks do we visit? (Brandenburg Gate, TV tower)
What else do we do in the city centre? (Spree, monuments)
When do we book the tickets? (today, tomorrow)

q.en: Hi Anna! Shall we go <g>to Berlin</g> next month? The capital is supposed to be great.

a.en:
I like that a lot.
We could go to the Brandenburg Gate first.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I would suggest that we then take a walk to the Spree.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
We could afterwards go to the city centre and look at the monuments.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Why don't we just book the train tickets today already?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We go to Berlin, go to the Brandenburg Gate, walk to the Spree, go to the city centre and book the train tickets today. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
You have planned a route for a walk through Berlin and would like to discuss it with a friend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Where do we start? (town hall, station)
What do we visit? (museum, bridge)
Where do we take a break? (café, park)

q.en: Hi Nina! I've planned a route for a walk through Berlin. Do you want to have a look at it?

a.en:
Yes, gladly.
We could start at the town hall.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Actually yes, but wouldn't it be better if we started at the station?
I have a suggestion: we walk from the station to the town hall.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
My suggestion would be that we then go to the museum.
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
How about if we afterwards cross the bridge to the café in the park?

a2.en: <r>Exactly, I think so too.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> We walk from the station to the town hall, then to the museum and over the bridge to the café in the park. <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r>

task.en:
You are a big fan of history and would like to plan a city tour with a friend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we visit?
Where do we eat?
What do we finish with?

q.en: Hi David! I'm a <g>big</g> fan of history. Can we plan a city tour?

a.en:
Yes, gladly.
We could visit a historical museum.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but I would also like to see a famous square.
I suggest that we go to the square first and then to the museum.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we look for a typical restaurant afterwards?
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
We could do it like this: at the end we walk through a beautiful park.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> first we go to the square and the museum, then we look for a typical restaurant, and at the end we walk through the park. That will definitely be an <g>interesting</g> day! <r>I'm already looking forward to it!</r> <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You would like to apply for an internship and need help preparing.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we practise first?
What do we write in the application?
When do we meet?

q.en: Hi Julia! I would like to apply for an internship. Can you help me prepare?

a.en:
Yes, gladly.
We could practise the job interview first.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Good idea, let's do that. I also still have to write my CV.
How about if we write it together afterwards?
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Let's write how motivated and committed you are.
How do you see that?

q2.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
We could do it like this: we meet tomorrow at three o'clock in my apartment.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we meet tomorrow at three o'clock at your place, practise the job interview first and then write the CV and the application. I'm sure you <g>will</g> <g>be</g> successful, Nina! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
Your son has a maths test tomorrow. You would like to plan the afternoon with your partner.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Who picks up the son?
Who helps with the homework?
What else do we practise?

q.en: Hi Anna! Our son has a maths test tomorrow. Can we plan the afternoon together?

a.en:
Yes, gladly.
We could do it like this: I pick him up from the after-school care, because I finish work earlier today.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Good idea, let's do that. I'm only home at five.
I would suggest that I help him with his homework then.
Does that work for you?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but he got a bad grade last time.
One idea would be that we practise maths afterwards.
How do you see that?

q2.en:
Right, I didn't think of that.
We could practise the tasks from the last test.
What do you think about that?

a2.en: <r>Agreed, that works well.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> I pick him up from the after-school care, you help him with his homework at five, and afterwards we practise the tasks from the last test together. <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
Tomorrow is your daughter's parent-teacher conference. You would like to prepare with your partner.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we talk about?
What do we ask the teacher?
When do we prepare?

q.en: Hi Julia! Tomorrow is our daughter's parent-teacher conference. Shall we prepare briefly?

a.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
Let's first think about what we want to talk about.
What do you think of that?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well. I often get annoyed about the noise in the class.
We could talk to the teacher about it.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
That sounds good, but I've been waiting for the maths grade for a long time.
One idea would be that we also ask the teacher about the grade.
How do you see that?

q2.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
We could do it like this: this evening we prepare together for the conversation.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we talk to the teacher about the noise and ask about the maths grade. This evening we prepare together. I'm already <g>looking forward to</g> the conversation, Alex! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
The children have an important test next week. You would like to plan a study time with your partner.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
How long do we study each day?
How often do we take breaks?
Where do we study?

q.en: Hi Julia! The children have an important test next week. Shall we plan a study time?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
We could study together for two hours every day.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but we should also plan enough breaks so that they can concentrate.
I have a suggestion: we take a five-minute break every thirty minutes.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we study at our place?
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the children always want to play at your place.
How about if we go to the library?
Would that be okay for you?

a2.en: <r>Good idea, let's do that.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we study for two hours every day in the library and take a five-minute break every thirty minutes. Then they will surely be well <g>prepared for</g> the test, Mark! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
Your daughter is very gifted at maths. You would like to plan the application for a support programme with your partner.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Who do we talk to first?
What do we need to prepare?
By when do we apply?

q.en: Hi Julia! Our daughter is very gifted at maths. Shall we apply for a place in the support programme?

a.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
We could talk to the class teacher first.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well. We also have to prepare the documents.
I suggest that we take her last report card and her maths tests with us.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
Exactly, I think so too.
My suggestion would be that we send off the application by Wednesday.
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
That doesn't suit me so well, I'm afraid, because the class teacher only has time on Thursday.
How about if we send off the application by next Monday?
Would that be okay for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we talk to the class teacher on Thursday, take the report card and the maths tests with us, and send off the application by next Monday. I'm sure this <g>will be</g> a great experience for our daughter, Anna! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and your flatmate have been arguing a lot lately. You would like to plan a calm conversation.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When do we talk?
Where do we talk?
What do we write down beforehand?

q.en: Hi Julia! We've been arguing a lot lately. Shall we talk about it calmly sometime?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
We could talk this evening after dinner.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but I'm still angry, so I need some time.
I have a suggestion: we wait until tomorrow morning, then we'll be calmer.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Okay, I understand. Tomorrow morning works for me too.
How about if we sit down in the kitchen?
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
We could do it like this: each of us writes down beforehand what bothers us.
What do you think about that?

a2.en: <r>Agreed, that works well.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we talk tomorrow morning in the kitchen, and each of us writes down beforehand what bothers us. I think this <g>will help</g> both of us improve the mood, Mark! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You would like to borrow a car from a friend for tomorrow.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
How do we ask politely?
What should we pay attention to?
When do we return the car?

q.en: Hi David! I need to ask you for a favour. Can you listen to me for a moment?

a.en:
Sure, no problem.
Let's talk about it right now.
What do you think of that?

q1.en:
Good idea, let's do that. Could you lend me your car for tomorrow?
I have a suggestion: I'll drive carefully and return it with a full tank.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Yes, gladly. When it rains, though, you should be especially careful.
We could do it like this: you pick up the keys from me tomorrow morning.
Does that work for you?

q2.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
I suggest that I bring the car back tomorrow evening at seven o'clock.
Would that be okay for you?

a2.en: <r>Agreed, that works well.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> you pick up the keys from me tomorrow morning and bring the car back tomorrow evening at seven o'clock. I trust you. Thank you <g>for</g> asking so respectfully, Nina! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
There have been some misunderstandings in the team recently. You would like to plan a team-building event with a colleague.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we do?
What do we talk about?
When does it take place?

q.en: Hi Anna! There have been some misunderstandings in the team recently. Shall we plan a team-building event?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
We could organise a joint cooking event.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but we should also talk about tolerance and criticism.
I have a suggestion: we talk about it during the shared meal.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Let's also think about how we can help each other better.
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Perfect, that's how we'll do it.
We could do it like this: we plan the event for next Friday afternoon.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we cook together next Friday afternoon and talk about tolerance, criticism and mutual help over the meal. I think this <g>will help</g> us make up and work together better, Alex! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You and your flatmate have had a long-running argument about the kitchen. You would like to sort it out.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What exactly is the point of contention?
Who gives in on what?
How do we record the solution?

q.en: Hi Mark! We've been arguing about the kitchen for a long time. <g>Let's</g> <g>sort</g> this out.

a.en:
Good idea, let's do that.
We could first say what the point of conflict is for us.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well. It annoys me that the kitchen is often dirty.
I suggest that I clean during the week.
What do you think of that?

a1.en:
That's okay with me, but we would still have to clarify who cleans at the weekend.
We could do it like this: I clean at the weekend.
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Perfect, that's how we'll do it.
We could do it like this: we write the plan down and hang it in the kitchen.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> you clean during the week, I clean at the weekend, and we hang the plan in the kitchen. Then we'll finally have peace at home again, Nina! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You have spent too much time on the screen and would like to plan a day without your phone with a friend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
Which day do we choose?
Which devices do we leave at home?
What do we do instead?

q.en: Hi Anna! I've spent too much time on the screen. Shall we have a day without our phones?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
We could choose next Sunday for it.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I suggest that we leave our phone, tablet and laptop at home.
What do you think of that?

a1.en:
That's okay with me, but we would still have to clarify what we do instead.
How about if we go to the big park nearby and have a picnic there?
How do you see that?

q2.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
We could do it like this: we meet at ten o'clock at the park entrance.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> next Sunday we leave our phone, tablet and laptop at home, meet at ten o'clock at the park entrance and have a picnic in the big park. I'm already <g>looking forward to</g> a day without screens, Nina! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
Your laptop is broken, the display no longer works. You would like to go to the shop with a friend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we check first?
What do we bring?
When do we go?

q.en: Hi David! My laptop is broken, the display doesn't work anymore. Will you come with me to the shop?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
We could check the warranty first.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but the broken laptop is already two years old. The warranty may have expired.
I have a suggestion: we ask a technician anyway.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
I suggest that we take the laptop, the charging cable and the warranty card with us.
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Perfect, that's how we'll do it.
We could do it like this: we go straight to customer service tomorrow morning.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we check the warranty first, take the laptop, the charging cable and the warranty card with us, and go to customer service tomorrow morning. I hope they <g>can</g> <g>repair</g> the laptop quickly, Alex! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You've heard about an app for learning German and would like to try it with a friend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we check before downloading?
What goal do we set ourselves?
When do we practise together?

q.en: Hi Julia! I've heard about an app for learning German. Do you want to try it with me?

a.en:
Yes, gladly.
We could read the reviews first.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Good idea, let's do that. That's a good tip.
Let's also check whether the app is free.
What do you think about that?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
My suggestion would be that we set ourselves a daily goal of ten minutes.
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
We could do it like this: we practise together every evening at eight o'clock.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we read the reviews first, check whether the app is free, and then download it. Every evening at eight o'clock we practise for ten minutes together. I'm already <g>excited about</g> our progress, Nina! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You've heard about a repair café in a forum and would like to go there with a friend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When do we go?
What do we bring to pass the time?
Where do we meet?

q.en: Hi Mark! I heard about a repair café in a forum. Do you want to go there with me?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
We could go there together on Saturday.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but the repair will certainly take a long time.
I have a suggestion: we bring a book to read.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Let's also take a card game with us.
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Perfect, that's how we'll do it.
We could do it like this: we meet at ten o'clock in front of the café.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we go there together on Saturday, bring a book and a card game, and meet at ten o'clock in front of the café. I hope the repair goes well, Alex! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
The shirt you bought doesn't fit you. You would like to exchange it with a friend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When do we go?
What do we bring?
What do we ask the salesperson?

q.en: Hi Nina! The shirt I bought doesn't fit me. Will you come with me to exchange it?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
We could go to the shop tomorrow afternoon.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Good idea, let's do that. I hope we meet the saleswoman who sold me the shirt.
We could take the shirt and the receipt with us.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
Let's ask for a size that fits you better.
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Perfect, that's how we'll do it.
We could do it like this: we meet at two o'clock in front of the shop.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we meet tomorrow at two o'clock in front of the shop, take the shirt and the receipt with us, and ask for a different size. I hope they have a shirt <g>that</g> <g>fits</g> you better, Alex! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
There is a new art exhibition at the museum. You would like to see it with a friend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
When do we go?
What do we want to look at?
Where do we meet?

q.en: Hi David! There's a new art exhibition at the museum. Shall we go see it together?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
We could go there on Saturday morning.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but I mainly want to see the famous painting in the middle.
I have a suggestion: we stop by there first.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we look at the modern sculptures at the back afterwards?
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
We could do it like this: we meet at eleven o'clock at the entrance of the museum.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we meet on Saturday morning at eleven o'clock at the entrance, first look at the famous painting in the middle and then at the modern sculptures at the back. I'm already <g>excited about</g> the exhibition, Anna! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You would like to order an original gift online and need help from a friend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we order?
How do we have it delivered?
How do we pay?

q.en: Hi Anna! I would like to order an original gift online. Can you help me choose?

a.en:
Yes, gladly.
We could first look for a special song poster.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but I'm never at home during the day.
I have a suggestion: we have the parcel delivered to the parcel locker.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
My suggestion would be that we pay by card.
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
We could do it like this: we split the costs in half.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we order the song poster, have the parcel delivered to the parcel locker, pay by card and split the costs. Then the gift will soon be waiting <g>in the</g> parcel locker, Nina! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You have found an old drawer and a basket. You would like to make something new out of them with a friend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we make from the drawer?
What do we make from the basket?
When do we start?

q.en: Hi Julia! I found an old drawer and a basket. Shall we make something new out of them?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
We could build a small shelf out of the drawer.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but we should also make something out of the basket.
I have a suggestion: we put soft cushions in it and make a comfortable bed for my dog out of it.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well.
How about if we buy the cushions cheaply at the flea market?
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
We could do it like this: we meet on Saturday at ten o'clock at the flea market and start afterwards.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we build a small shelf from the drawer, make a dog bed from the basket, buy the cushions at the flea market and start on Saturday. I'm already looking forward to reusing old things, Alex! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You think you want to become an electrician. You would like to plan with a friend how to achieve that.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
How do we find a training position?
What are my strengths and weaknesses?
What do we do next?

q.en: Hi Mark! I think I'll <g>become</g> an electrician. Can you help me plan that?

a.en:
Sounds great, let's do that.
We could first search online for training positions.
What do you think?

q1.en:
That sounds good, but I hope I will really become a good electrician.
I have a suggestion: we first write down my strengths.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Agreed, that works well. You will certainly become a good electrician.
Let's also write down your weaknesses honestly.
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Perfect, that's how we'll do it.
We could do it like this: we call a company tomorrow and ask about an internship.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we search the internet for apprenticeships, write down your strengths and weaknesses, and call a company tomorrow. I think you will <g>become</g> a great electrician, David! <r>See you then!</r>

task.en:
You have a job interview next week and would like to prepare with a friend.

Plan together with your conversation partner how you would like to do this.

These points will help you:
What do we practise?
Which key qualifications do I mention?
When do we meet?

q.en: Hi Anna! I have a job interview next week. Can you give me some advice?

a.en:
Yes, gladly.
We could practise typical questions first.
What do you think?

q1.en:
Good idea, let's do that. Could you give me an example of a typical question?
I have a suggestion: I'll think about my key qualifications beforehand.
How do you like that?

a1.en:
Yes, gladly. A typical question is: Why do you want this job?
My suggestion would be that you name your key qualifications with examples as you answer.
Are you okay with that?

q2.en:
Perfect, let's do it that way.
We could do it like this: we meet tomorrow evening at seven o'clock and practise for an hour.
Does that work for you?

a2.en: <r>I like that very much.</r> <r>So, here's what we'll do:</r> we meet tomorrow evening at seven o'clock, practise typical questions, and you name your key qualifications with examples. You <g>should</g> get a good night's sleep before the interview, Alex! <r>See you then!</r>
